title: Castiel framework completion
order_rules: castiel is an abstract framework repository: write specifications only. No implementation code, no pseudo-code, no commands, no library or product names.
Deliverables are Markdown (plus the two plain-text version files where named). Illustrative data may appear only as clearly labelled informative field tables or examples, never as program logic.

Every normative statement is one numbered clause with a unique ID of the form PREFIX-file:rule, as in the existing component specs. Never reuse or renumber an existing ID; mark withdrawn clauses RETIRED.
Use MUST, SHOULD and MAY (RFC 2119 / RFC 8174) only inside normative clauses. User interface is an implementation concern: at most a normative SHOULD.
Be platform- and language-agnostic: name no cloud provider, operating system, programming language or product.
When replacing an existing file, return the complete file and keep every existing clause ID unchanged.
Record each design choice you had to make as a DP-nn item under Findings, for the operator to ratify. Do not invent facts about existing specs: cite clause IDs.
Use the terminology of the existing specs. Retired names (OS/7, Kernel Map, operator map, amk-registry, host-ai-kernel-prompt) appear only in a deprecation table.
